correctness.rationale: For general 2x2 Hurwitz B, the real harmonic response has complex amplitude (adj(-B)v+i omega v)/det(i omega I-B). Symmetry of H makes the averaged quadratic form an affine function of omega^2 divided by a strictly positive denominator, hence at most one sign change. In the explicit real-analytic example, strict g derivative bound, equilibrium, B/v/H and rational coefficient were reconstructed with exact rational identities. Analytic epsilon dependence and half-period symmetry justify O(epsilon^4); at the critical frequency the sign is explicitly left undecided. Standalone verify.py passes.

value.rationale: The one-crossing law constrains the complete frequency-axis sign topology of weakly forced throughput for every admissible two-site model and provides an explicit threshold from equilibrium/curvature data. The analytic example shows strict sign reversal with a uniquely optimal gain frequency under a single fixed waveform, making the bound exact and operationally interpretable rather than a finite one-off computation. It separates frequency selection from arbitrary-input Jacobi eigenvalue realizability.
